title: Proper direct image of unbounded ind-constructible complexes
statement:
Let $\Lambda$, $p$, $d$ be as in [det-proper-unbounded-window-bounded-below] and $K\in\Dic(X,\Lambda)$
arbitrary. For each $q$ there is $N$ such that for $n\geq N$ the map
$\mathcal H^q(Rp_*K)\to\mathcal H^q(Rp_*\tau_{\geq-n}K)$ is an isomorphism. Consequently
$Rp_*K\in\Dic(Y,\Lambda)$, $Rp_*\Dic^{\leq b}(X,\Lambda)\subset\Dic^{\leq b+2d+1}(Y,\Lambda)$ and
$Rp_*\Dic^{\geq a}(X,\Lambda)\subset\Dic^{\geq a}(Y,\Lambda)$.

external.place: *Milnor.* By [sk-prop-pe-milnor], there is an exact sequence of sheaves $$ 0\to R^1\varprojlim_n\mathcal H^{q-1}(Rp_*\tau_{\geq-n}K)\to\mathcal H^q(Rp_*K)\to\varprojlim_n\mathcal H^q(Rp_*\tau_{\geq-n}K)\to0. $$ The tower in degree $q-1$ is eventually constant, so its $R^1\varprojlim$ vanishes (description as $\coker(1-T)$ on the product, solved successively); the tower in degree $q$ is eventually

proof.text:
Work throughout with the pulled-back condensed coefficient ring sheaves $\Lambda_X,\Lambda_Y$ and their module categories, as in [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]; no discrete-coefficient replacement is made. By [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and the sheafified sectionwise tensor formula in [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], these module objects are exactly sheaves of modules over the ring sheaves: an action gives compatible bilinear maps on sections, and conversely compatible sectionwise actions factor uniquely through the sheafified tensor product. The unit and associativity identities agree in both descriptions. We may work on small site models in the fixed universe of these coefficient sheaves. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] their module categories are Grothendieck abelian, and [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective] gives K-injective resolutions in both categories. Put $A_n=\tau_{\geq-n}K$ and $L_n=Rp_*A_n$ for $n\in\mathbf N$. By [det-pe-products-derived], products in these ambient derived categories exist and are represented by termwise products. The adjunction [def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction] shows that $Rp_*$ preserves these products, including their projections: for every $B$ on $Y$ and every family $(C_i)$ on $X$, the natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(B,Rp_*\prod_i C_i)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Lp^*B,\prod_i C_i)\cong\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(Lp^*B,C_i)\cong\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(B,Rp_*C_i)$$
are the product universal property. Moreover [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] applies to the K-injective right derived functor of the module direct image, which is additive by [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], and gives its compatibility with shifts and distinguished triangles.

source.place: Limit presentation: products and exactness of the derived direct image

proof.text:
By [det-pe-left-complete-iso], the canonical truncation cone identifies $K$ with $R\varprojlim_n A_n$. Apply [lem-pc-homotopy-limit-map] to this cone and the triangulated, product-preserving functor $Rp_*$ of Step 1. It gives a homotopy-limit cone $Rp_*K\to L_n$, so
$$Rp_*K\simeq R\varprojlim_n L_n.$$
The maps to $L_n$ in this presentation are precisely $Rp_*(K\to A_n)$, because the cited lemma maps the whole cone, including its projection maps. In particular, writing $P=\prod_nL_n$, the image cone is the distinguished triangle $Rp_*K\xrightarrow{u}P\xrightarrow{1-T}P\to(Rp_*K)[1]$ of [def-weil-derived-limit], with $\operatorname{pr}_n u=Rp_*(K\to A_n)$.

source.place: Limit presentation: the truncation cone and its direct image

proof.text:
The definition of $\Dic$ and its truncation closure in [det-ambient-ind-derived-sums] ensure that $A_n$ and the sheaf $\mathcal H^{-n-1}(K)$ placed in degree $-n-1$ belong to $\Dic$. The latter assertion also follows directly from its having only this one nonzero, ind-constructible cohomology sheaf. Apply [lem-pc-derived-lower-truncation-step-triangle] with integer $n+1$: its canonical triangle is
$$F_n:=\mathcal H^{-n-1}(K)[n+1]\longrightarrow A_{n+1}\longrightarrow A_n\longrightarrow F_n[1].$$
The bounded-below theorem [det-proper-unbounded-window-bounded-below], applied to $F_n$, puts $Rp_*F_n$ in degrees $[-n-1,2d-n]$. Apply $Rp_*$, which is triangulated by Step 1. By [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], the kernel and cokernel of $\mathcal H^r(L_{n+1})\to\mathcal H^r(L_n)$ vanish if $\mathcal H^r(Rp_*F_n)=\mathcal H^{r+1}(Rp_*F_n)=0$. Fix $q\in\mathbf Z$ and take $N_0=\max\{0,2d-q+2\}$. For $n\geq N_0$ one has $2d-n<q-1$; hence the required vanishings hold for both $r=q$ and $r=q-1$. Both cohomology towers therefore have isomorphisms as transitions from $N_0$ onwards.

source.place: Eventual constancy: truncation triangle, shifted bound, and long exact sequence

proof.text: Here is the elementary calculation needed for either eventual tower. Let $t_i:M_{i+1}\to M_i$ be isomorphisms for $i\geq N_0$. For any tuple $y=(y_i)$ of sections, set $x_{N_0}=0$, recursively set $x_i=y_i+t_i x_{i+1}$ for $i<N_0$ going downwards, and set $x_{i+1}=t_i^{-1}(x_i-y_i)$ for $i\geq N_0$ going upwards. Each coordinate is a finite linear expression in the $y_i$, natural under restriction, so this defines a morphism of product sheaves with $(1-T)x=y$. Thus $1-T$ is split surjective and its cokernel is zero. By the sectionwise inverse-limit description [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit], projection $\varprojlim_i M_i\to M_n$ is an isomorphism for every $n\geq N_0$: a section in $M_n$ extends uniquely downwards by the $t_i$ and upwards by their inverses. These extensions commute with restrictions. This uses actual inverses only on the tail; no surjectivity is assumed for the finitely many earlier transitions.

source.place: Milnor: explicit solution of 1-T and the inverse-limit projections

proof.text:
Use the image Roos triangle of Step 2 directly in the derived category, so no choice of a strict complex-level representative of the tower is needed. By [det-pe-products-derived], $H^r(P)=\prod_n H^r(L_n)$ naturally in the projections, and $H^r(1-T)$ is $1-T$ on these products. By [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], its cohomology sequence contains
$$\prod_nH^{q-1}(L_n)\xrightarrow{1-T}\prod_nH^{q-1}(L_n)\to H^q(Rp_*K)\xrightarrow{H^q(u)}\prod_nH^q(L_n)\xrightarrow{1-T}\prod_nH^q(L_n).$$
Exactness therefore identifies the kernel of $H^q(u)$ with the cokernel of the first $1-T$ and its image with the kernel of the last $1-T$. That last kernel is $\varprojlim_n H^q(L_n)$ by the compatible-tuples description [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. We have obtained precisely the Milnor short exact sequence
$$0\to\operatorname{coker}\!\left(\prod_nH^{q-1}(L_n)\xrightarrow{1-T}\prod_nH^{q-1}(L_n)\right)\to H^q(Rp_*K)\to\varprojlim_nH^q(L_n)\to0.$$
Steps 3 and 4 kill the left term and identify every projection of the right term to $H^q(L_n)$ for $n\geq N_0$ as an isomorphism. The composite with that projection is $H^q(\operatorname{pr}_n u)=H^q(Rp_*(K\to A_n))$ by Step 2. Thus the asserted canonical map is an isomorphism with $N=N_0$.

source.place: Milnor: its short exact sequence derived from the image Roos triangle, with the canonical projections retained

proof.text: For each fixed $q$, choose $n\geq N_0$ as in Step 5. The bounded-below object $A_n$ is in $\Dic$ by [det-ambient-ind-derived-sums], and [det-proper-unbounded-window-bounded-below] gives $\mathcal H^q(L_n)\in\IndCons(Y,\Lambda)$. Step 5 identifies this with $\mathcal H^q(Rp_*K)$, proving $Rp_*K\in\Dic(Y,\Lambda)$ by the definition of $\Dic$ in [det-ambient-ind-derived-sums]. If $K$ has no cohomology above $b$, neither does $A_n$, since canonical truncation retains only the original cohomology in its retained degrees. The same bounded-below theorem then gives $\mathcal H^q(L_n)=0$ for $q>b+2d+1$, and Step 5 gives this vanishing for $Rp_*K$. Finally, if $K$ has no cohomology below $a$, it is already bounded below, so the lower amplitude bound is directly the last application of [det-proper-unbounded-window-bounded-below].

Generic Grothendieck K-injective-resolution existence verifies both ambient categories meet the triangulated right-derived tool hypotheses.
